subject: English
passage:
The following text is from Louisa May Alcott's 1868 novel Little Women. Beth, a shy sixteen-year-old girl, has been invited to attend a grand party with her more outgoing sister Amy.

Beth shrank from the thought of the evening's festivities.

"Oh, Amy," she said quietly one afternoon, wringing her hands as her sister showed her the elegant invitation, "I simply cannot imagine myself at such a gathering. There will be so many people, and they will all expect me to be witty and charming. I would much rather spend the evening at home with my music."

"Nonsense," declared Amy, whose confidence never wavered. "It will be delightful, and you must come. These are precisely the sort of people worth knowing, Beth. You can't hide away forever."
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To illustrate that Beth has recently become more anxious about social situations
choices.B: To describe a heated disagreement that Beth and Amy frequently have
choices.C: To show that Beth and Amy have very different temperaments
choices.D: To highlight Amy's frustration with Beth's reluctance to attend social events

explanation:
Choice C is the best answer because the text shows that Beth and Amy have very different temperaments. Beth 'shrank from the thought of the evening's festivities' and expresses her fears, saying she 'cannot imagine' herself at such a gathering and 'would much rather spend the evening at home with my music.' In contrast, Amy's 'confidence never wavered'—she dismisses Beth's concerns as 'Nonsense' and encourages her to attend, declaring 'It will be delightful.' This episode illustrates that Beth is shy and retiring while Amy is bold and sociable, demonstrating their fundamentally different temperaments.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect because the text presents Beth's social anxiety as a basic personality trait, not as a recent development, and never indicates when this characteristic emerged.
